description: Elementary Grades 1-2 deterministic misconception and remediation catalog. Each entry maps to a canonical mathematical concept and provides application-owned classification rules and remediation guidance.

misconceptions.name: Skips numbers when counting
misconceptions.remediation: Use a number line or hundred chart to rehearse counting by ones from a given start number.

misconceptions.name: Compares multi-digit numbers by digit count or first digit only
misconceptions.remediation: Compare place values from left to right; use base-ten models to justify the result.

misconceptions.name: Confuses teen numbers with tens
misconceptions.remediation: Build the number with base-ten blocks and name the tens and ones separately.

misconceptions.name: Reads digits by face value only
misconceptions.remediation: Use a place-value mat: label tens and ones columns and place counters.

misconceptions.name: Ignores zeros in three-digit numbers
misconceptions.remediation: Decompose the number with base-ten blocks and record each place, including zeros.

misconceptions.name: Counts all objects instead of counting on
misconceptions.remediation: Use a number line or ten-frame: start at the larger addend and count on.

misconceptions.name: Always subtracts smaller digit from larger digit regardless of position
misconceptions.remediation: Model the minuend with counters and remove the subtrahend; compare to a number line.

misconceptions.name: Does not decompose to make a ten
misconceptions.remediation: Practice making ten with a ten-frame; decompose the smaller addend to reach ten first.

misconceptions.name: Adds tens and ones independently without regrouping
misconceptions.remediation: Use base-ten blocks to combine ones, regroup ten ones as a ten, then combine tens.

misconceptions.name: Decomposes the wrong place value in subtraction
misconceptions.remediation: Model the minuend with base-ten blocks; trade one ten for ten ones when needed.

misconceptions.name: Relies only on keywords rather than the situation
misconceptions.remediation: Act out the problem with objects; identify whether the total increases, decreases, or is compared.

misconceptions.name: Solves only the first step of a two-step problem
misconceptions.remediation: Restate the question; solve one step, then use that answer to complete the second step.

misconceptions.name: Treats the equal sign as a prompt for an answer rather than a balance
misconceptions.remediation: Use a balance model: both sides must have the same value. Check by computing each side.

misconceptions.name: Confuses hour and minute hands
misconceptions.remediation: Label hands: the shorter hand shows the hour; the longer hand shows minutes.

misconceptions.name: Counts minute marks as single minutes
misconceptions.remediation: Count by fives around the clock face; each number represents five minutes.

misconceptions.name: Confuses coin size with value
misconceptions.remediation: Sort coins by value; use a coin-value chart and count from highest to lowest.

misconceptions.name: Subtracts lengths without attending to units
misconceptions.remediation: Measure both objects with the same unit; subtract only after units match.

misconceptions.name: Does not recognize shapes in nonstandard orientations
misconceptions.remediation: Rotate shapes and trace sides; focus on defining attributes, not orientation or size.

misconceptions.name: Counts parts without checking equal size
misconceptions.remediation: Fold paper shapes to confirm equal shares before naming the fraction.

misconceptions.name: Identifies a different step size in a pattern
misconceptions.remediation: Find the difference between consecutive terms; verify by continuing the pattern.
